test_title: PYST 22: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 19 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced a cap on the size of the State Council of Ministers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003** introduced a cap on the size of the State Council of Ministers.
 
• According to this amendment, the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the State Council of Ministers cannot exceed **15% of the total strength of the State Legislative Assembly**.
 
• This amendment was enacted to ensure efficient governance and to curb unnecessary expansion of ministries, which could lead to financial burdens and administrative inefficiencies.
 
• The amendment also introduced provisions for disqualification of legislators under the **anti-defection law**, strengthening the political structure and promoting accountability.
 
• The **anti-defection law**, added as the **Tenth Schedule** of the Constitution, was amended to ensure that defecting legislators lose their right to hold any ministerial position.
 
• This amendment applies to both the Union Council of Ministers and the State Council of Ministers, bringing uniformity to the structure and size of government across the country.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:**

 
 
• This amendment was implemented to promote efficient governance and reduce the financial burden caused by oversized councils of ministers.
 
• It introduced a **mandatory cap of 15%** on the size of councils of ministers at both the central and state levels.
 
• It strengthened the **anti-defection law** by disqualifying defectors from holding ministerial positions, ensuring political stability.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Defection Law:**
 
 
• Added to the Constitution as the **Tenth Schedule** by the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985**.
 
• It seeks to prevent political defections by disqualifying members of the legislature who switch parties.
 
• The **91st Constitutional Amendment Act** further strengthened this law by including provisions to disqualify defectors from holding ministerial positions.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the 91st Amendment:**
 
 
• Promotes **transparent governance** by limiting the size of councils of ministers.
 
• Ensures financial prudence by reducing unnecessary expenditure on salaries and allowances for ministers.
 
• Encourages political accountability by preventing defectors from being rewarded with ministerial positions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background of the 91st Amendment:**

 
 
• Before the 91st Amendment, there was no cap on the size of councils of ministers, leading to excessive expansion and inefficiencies.
 
• The amendment was introduced in response to growing concerns about governance inefficiencies and financial burdens caused by oversized ministries.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Amendments:**
 
 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:** Introduced provisions for **Panchayati Raj**, establishing a three-tier system of governance at the local level.
 
• **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988:** Reduced the **minimum voting age** from 21 to 18 years for Lok Sabha and state assembly elections.
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:** Known as the **Mini Constitution**, it brought significant changes to the Constitution, including the addition of the words **“Socialist” and “Secular”** to the Preamble.
